result.reasoning:
TRIED TO REFUTE, FAILED. The core claim holds and I reproduced wrong output from my own scripts (not the reporter's).

WHAT IS CONFIRMED
1. `_lexi`'s band is a quota, not a condition. `_pct_rank` (ops_ext.py:226) is `argsort(argsort(v, stable=True), stable=True)+1`, i.e. an ordinal rank with ties broken by column index; `(rx > lo) & (rx <= hi)` therefore always selects exactly 20%/40% of the valid names, however many names genuinely satisfy "the highest 20% of x". Measured band width at tie_share 0.00/0.50/0.85/0.929/0.99/1.00 = 20.0% every time; at tie_share 0.929, 129 of the 200 pushed names are tied at the minimum (independently reproduces the reporter's 12.9pp).
2. Unambiguous wrong output, no data assumptions needed: with x CONSTANT ("the highest 20% of x" is empty), `cs_last_high20` still pushes 20% of the universe to the book floor — exactly the 200 highest-index columns, the same set every day — and `cs_first_low40` still promotes 40%. Permuting the column order moves 304 of 1000 names across the line.
3. It changes the numbers the F103 table is read for. Same expression, same data, 12 different symbol orders, scored with Partura's own books.py (`long_short_weights` + `long_book`, 15bp): long_ann spread 0.0225 at N=1200, 0.0223 at N=2400, 0.0103 at N=4700; long_sharpe spread 1.18/1.02/0.71. The increment these rows exist to measure is +1.27pp ann / +0.28 Sharpe (h_K_ex_new +16.67%/2.506 vs k_known +15.40%/2.224, runs/F103_amt_dw_decay/sweep_s3.json). The symbol-order artefact is the same size or larger at a realistic universe size.
4. Expressions verified in the run files: h_K_ex_new = `cs_last_high20(neg(cross_mean(day_std(Amt),30)), neg(cross_valid_count(day_last(Close),241)))`; F102 seg_new_p = `cs_first_low40(cross_sum(pow_2(day_kurt(nt_ts_autocorr_s1(Ret,3))),15), cross_valid_count(day_last(Close),241))` (−13.47%/−2.803, as quoted); h_K_ex_both nests the two screens; k_known_xfrozen +18.54%/3.154 vs h_K_ex_both +18.10%/3.158, so the report is right that the headline is layer 1 and the contaminated part is the layer-2 increment.
5. An extra, data-independent amplifier the report missed: the production view starts ON the store's first day (`research.warmed_view`: d0 = max(0, base.d0 − warmup) = 0, since SPLITS["full"][0] = 20180102 = the store's first date), so `rolling_windows`' NaN left-pad caps `cross_valid_count(.,241)` for the first 240 trading days of TRAIN. Measured tie block there: 100% of valid names on days 0–5, 98.8% at day 60, 96.7% at day 239. Over that quarter of train the "剔次新" band is almost entirely column-order determined no matter what the halt rate is.
6. Real-data corroboration from runs/F103_amt_dw_decay/anatomy_s3.json (held_share = the book's weight share): h_K_ex_new holds 0.0038 in 上市:不足250日 vs k_known's 0.0617 (universe 0.0709) — the quota covers the whole young segment and spills over. And 流通市值:最低20% held_share is 0.5019 (k_known, no screen) → 0.4281 (h_K_ex_new) → 0.3677 (h3_K_ex_age_cont, the non-saturating age screen): the extra ~13% the quota pushes carries almost none of the size tilt that the genuinely next-youngest names carry, i.e. it is orthogonal to the covariate's semantics. That is what an arbitrary block looks like.
7. The report is RIGHT to list h3_K_ex_age_cont, though not for the reason given. `cross_age` hands every name finite on the view's first day the identical value t+10000, so its tie block is "listed before 20180102" (~64% of the final panel). The youngest-20% band clears that block only once ~20% of the panel has listed inside the view, i.e. not until ~2022. Simulated on the production shape (1942 days, 5400 names, 3480 pre-view): pushed-from-the-tie-block = 16.1% of the universe in mid-2018, 13.0% at end-2018, 7.5% at end-2019, 2.7% at end-2020, 0 from 2022 on; over utrain, 24.3% of the cells it pushes are decided by column index.

WHERE THE REPORT OVERSTATES (does not change the verdict)
- The 12.9pp figure assumes count<241 ⟺ recently listed. A halt also writes a null row (alphacube/calculate.py:248 "lifecycle_rule: outside=no row; suspended=row with null") and `cross_valid_count`'s own docstring says a small count means "recently suspended". With clustered 8-day halts at 0.1%/0.3%/1%/2%/5% of stock-days, the share of the universe decided by column index measures 9.8%/4.8%/9.9%/0.9%/7.6% — the mechanism never disappears (an integer count always has a tie block straddling the cut) but the exact 12.9pp is calibration-dependent. The anatomy evidence in (6) favours a large block, so 12.9pp is plausible, not established.
- "每一天都是同一批" holds only at a zero halt rate.
- I found no evidence for the implicit worry that the arbitrary block is board-skewed (it would be if the store's symbol array were code-sorted, since 688xxx/8xxxxx are the highest codes and 科创板 is the best segment at +4.12%): h_K_ex_new's 科创板 held_share 0.0219 is close to the pure-age screen's 0.0246, so no extra suppression is visible. I could not read the store's symbol order locally — worth checking before claiming it.

THE SUGGESTED FIX IS WRONG — see corrected_fix.

result.corrected_fix:
The defect is real but BOTH halves of the suggested fix are wrong; use the patch below instead.

WHY THE SUGGESTED FIX FAILS
`thr = nanquantile(x, hi); band = x >= thr` for cs_last_high20 (lo=0.8, hi=1.0):
- charitable reading (the band's lower edge, q=0.8): nanquantile(neg(count), 0.8) = −241.0, which IS the tied value, so `x >= thr` is true for EVERY name. Measured: 1000/1000 = 100.0%. Shifting the whole universe by −1 leaves the ordering unchanged, so the screen becomes a total no-op and h_K_ex_new collapses onto k_known. The same for the low side: nanquantile(count, 0.4) = 241 → `x <= thr` → 100%.
- literal reading (q = hi = 1.0): thr = max(x) → the band is the single youngest name, 1/1000 = 0.1%.
Neither gives the promised "真次新只有 7% 时就只剔 7%". A `>` instead of `>=` happens to give 7.1% here only because the block sits at the extreme; on a panel where the straddling block is not at the extreme the same expression silently flips between "whole block in" and "whole block out". And `nanquantile` on the day axis of a (days, stocks) panel is also 100x the cost of the sort already being done.
Changing `_pct_rank` to average/min/max ranks (the other half of the suggestion) does remove the order dependence, but it has two side effects the report does not account for: (a) `_lexi` uses `_pct_rank` for its OWN output `ry`, so averaged ranks make tied y values produce tied signals and the book's boundary falls back to `long_short_weights`' column-order tie-break — breaking the cs_first_*/cs_last_* docstring promise that "every stock keeps a distinct value (no NaN, no ties)"; (b) `_pct_rank` is also called by `cs_bucket_rank`, `_buckets` (→ cs_bucket_demean, cs_bucket_zscore) and `cs_flip_by_state`, and cs_bucket_rank's `+ 1e-4 * _pct_rank(y, ok)` tie-breaker exists precisely "so no decile book hangs on symbol order".

CORRECTED FIX — leave `_pct_rank` untouched, make only the BAND in `_lexi` tie-block aware, so a tie block is in the band only as a whole:

    def _rank_block(x, ok):
        """(first, last) percentile rank of each cell's own tie block, in (0, 1]."""
        v = torch.where(ok, x, torch.full_like(x, torch.finfo(x.dtype).max))
        s, order = torch.sort(v, dim=-1, stable=True)
        s = s.contiguous()
        first = (torch.searchsorted(s, s, right=False) + 1).to(x.dtype)
        last = torch.searchsorted(s, s, right=True).to(x.dtype)
        n = ok.sum(-1, keepdim=True).to(x.dtype).clamp(min=1)
        lo = torch.empty_like(x).scatter_(-1, order, first) / n
        hi = torch.empty_like(x).scatter_(-1, order, last) / n
        return (torch.where(ok, lo, torch.full_like(x, NAN)),
                torch.where(ok, hi, torch.full_like(x, NAN)))

    def _lexi(y, x, lo, hi, shift):
        y, x = _f(y), _f(x)
        ok = torch.isfinite(y) & torch.isfinite(x)
        ry = _pct_rank(y, ok)                     # unchanged: ordinal, so the output stays tie-free
        bl, bh = _rank_block(x, ok)
        band = (bl > lo) & (bh <= hi)             # whole block inside (lo, hi], or not in the band
        return torch.where(ok, ry + shift * band.to(y.dtype), torch.full_like(y, NAN))

Verified (r7_patch.py, with 25% of cells NaN): byte-identical to today for every continuous x and all four band widths; exactly the 7.5% genuinely-short-of-241 names on the cited input (0 mature) vs today's 20.0% with 86 mature; pushed set invariant to symbol permutation; output still tie-free. It is strictly conservative in both directions — a straddling block is never split, so no name is ever excluded or promoted on the strength of its column index — and it is the same `searchsorted` trick `alphacube/metrics.py::_avg_ranks_t` already uses, so it costs one extra sort pass, not a nanquantile.

DOCSTRINGS: add to cs_first_*/cs_last_* that the band is "the tie blocks that fit entirely inside the quantile range", so the width is at most 20%/40% and shrinks when x saturates — and say explicitly that an x with a tie block spanning the cut yields a narrower band, which is the intended behaviour, not a bug.

ROWS TO RECOMPUTE (the report's list, corrected):
- keep: F103 h_K_ex_new, h_base_ex_new, h_K_ex_both, h3_K_ex_age_cont (the report is right to include it; the contamination is in 2018–2021, i.e. all of train), F103 seg_new_p / seg_new_m.
- ADD, same x family and same quota, the report missed them: F102 seg_new_p, seg_new_m, h_susp_excl (`cross_valid_count(pow_2(day_kurt(...)), 60)` — saturates at 60), h3_max60_age (`cross_age`), and F102 h3_K_ex_age_cont-equivalents in other factors' sweeps.
- do NOT recompute on this account: k_known_xfrozen, h_K_ex_frzrun, h3_K_ex_frz40, h3_K_ex_limitup, h3_K_ex_limitdn, h3_K_ex_coarse, scr_xhi_*, seg_lowliq_*, seg_hiliq_*, h_liq40_*. Their x is a k/240-grid ratio or a continuous liquidity level with no 80%+ tie block, so the quota is wide-by-design rather than order-dependent; the patch leaves them bit-identical. (Worth a one-off check that `cross_max(day_zero_ratio(Ret), 15)` has no large block at the 80th percentile, but nothing in the anatomy suggests one.)
- docs/new_operators.md: the cs_first_*/cs_last_* section.
- Separately worth a look (same `_pct_rank`, same saturating x, not in this finding): `h_K_bk_age` = the age-neutral row, since `_buckets` = ceil(_pct_rank(x)*10) on a 93%-tied x makes deciles 1–9 pure column-index slices of one tie block.
